response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM per), s1 AS (SELECT per.ordersmark, per.a, per.a - b1.v AS m1 FROM per, b1 WHERE per.a > b1.v), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.ordersmark, s1.a, s1.m1, s1.a - b2.v AS m2 FROM s1, b2 WHERE s1.a > b2.v) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_fill_size, AVG(m1) AS avg_margin_over_first_benchmark, AVG(m2) AS avg_margin_over_second_benchmark FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: The first benchmark, 'the average across all orders', is the mean of the per-order average fill sizes. Each order, including the NULL-reference group, counts once.
The second benchmark is the mean of the per-order averages of the orders that passed the first filter. Comparisons are strict (>). Fills with a NULL fillcount are ignored by AVG.
All executions with a NULL ordersmark form one group, treated as one 'order'.

alternatives.interpretation: The first benchmark is the average fillcount across all individual fill rows, not the mean of per-order averages. The second benchmark is still the mean of the surviving orders' averages.
alternatives.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(fillcount) AS v FROM orderexecutions), s1 AS (SELECT per.ordersmark, per.a, per.a - b1.v AS m1 FROM per, b1 WHERE per.a > b1.v), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.ordersmark, s1.a, s1.m1, s1.a - b2.v AS m2 FROM s1, b2 WHERE s1.a > b2.v) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_fill_size, AVG(m1) AS avg_margin_over_first_benchmark, AVG(m2) AS avg_margin_over_second_benchmark FROM s2
